title: New Sub-Scope Default Report Lifecycle Delivery
summary: make New sub-scope create an indexed report host, valid empty manifests, and an immediately usable default report
content_html:
New Sub-Scope Default Report Lifecycle Delivery

Status And Purpose

Active as SSR-2 after SSR-1 shipped the accepted default and customisation framework. SSR-2.0 is frozen below; mutation work has not started.

This delivery makes the existing New sub-scope lifecycle create the normal management surface needed to reach and populate that collection. The recreated external-local dotlineform scope and its projects sub-scope are the focused acceptance scenario, not a reason for Projects-specific lifecycle code.

Complete Outcome

One confirmed New sub-scope apply creates:

  • the configured one-level collection and confined source/output roots;
  • one ordinary parent-scope report document explicitly associated with that collection;
  • a parent index entry using the supplied collection title;
  • valid empty local manifest.json and manage-manifest.json projections;
  • refreshed parent docs/search and browser configuration; and
  • an exact management URL that opens the default report.

The empty report shows a normal zero-document state and exact-collection New. The user can create or import the first child without manually writing a host document or running a builder.

Fixed Boundaries

  • This delivery consumes SSR-1's default; it does not copy Analysis/Tags configuration or implement another report scaffold.
  • The host is an ordinary parent document, not a synthetic tree node or new route identity.
  • The lifecycle records one exact collection/host association and never reconstructs it from title, filename, active document, or URL text.
  • Creation uses the existing planned identity and atomic create-only boundary.
  • Post-commit rebuild or presentation failure returns committed identities and retries follow-through only; it cannot create a duplicate.
  • A new sub-scope omits customisation identity and therefore receives the default.
  • Child documents remain excluded from parent Index, Recently Edited, and search payloads.
  • Public visibility remains governed by existing scope and publication configuration.
  • Delete preview/apply accounts for the exact lifecycle-associated host and fails closed on detached, ambiguous, changed, or missing association state.

Delivery Checkpoints

[x] SSR-2.0 — Freeze Lifecycle Plan

  • [x] Trace current local, external-local, and public-parent preview/apply and delete paths.
  • [x] Freeze host front matter/body, planned identity, association owner, empty manifest pair, result fields, rebuilds, and final management URL.
  • [x] Define pre-commit versus committed follow-through failure responses.
  • [x] Define symmetric delete consequences and user-authored host-change presentation.

Checkpoint: preview names every identity, write, generated projection, refresh, navigation result, and deletion consequence. Stop before mutation work.

SSR-2.0 current trace

  • docs_sub_scope_lifecycle.py currently plans the same derived child source and output roots for local, external-local, and public parents. Public parents additionally receive their configured publication root. Create writes those roots and one config record; it allocates no document identity, writes no host or manifest, and runs no builder.
  • Current delete accepts any configured sub-scope, removes its child source, local output, and configured public projection, then removes the config record. It has no exact host association, host-change check, or parent discovery rebuild.
  • SubScopeDocsBuilder already owns the canonical empty manifest.json/manage-manifest.json pair as {"docs": []}. The parent docs builder owns the host by-ID payload, Index, Recent, and browser configs; the parent search builder owns the search row.
  • The browser currently submits only parent scope, sub-scope, and title. After apply it reloads configuration/capabilities, but it carries no planned host identity and does not refresh/select a returned parent document.

Frozen create contract

The form remains {parent_scope, sub_scope, title}. Preview allocates and returns planned_report_host_identity: {doc_id, added_date}. Apply must return that exact object; the service recomputes the complete plan and rejects a changed identity, stale config, or any path/source collision before writing.

The host is a root-level ordinary parent document at <parent source documents>/<doc_id>.md. It uses the supplied title and this source shape:

---
doc_id: <planned doc_id>
title: <supplied title>
added_date: <planned added_date>
last_updated: <planned added_date>
viewable: false
viewer_report: docs_subscope
viewer_report_access: local
viewer_report_subscope: <sub-scope id>
---
# <supplied title>

It has no parent_id, ui_status, customisation identity, or copied report configuration. Local parents omit viewable; public parents retain the ordinary document-create default of viewable: false. Public visibility and later report promotion therefore remain explicit existing workflows.

The new sub-scope config record owns the exact lifecycle association:

{
  "sub_scope": "projects",
  "title": "Projects",
  "public_projection": null,
  "lifecycle": {
    "tool_id": "docs-viewer-scope-lifecycle",
    "report_host_doc_id": "d-*",
    "report_host_source_revision": "sha256:*"
  }
}

The normalized config validates this strict object. Absence means a manually configured collection, not an association to infer. New records omit report_customisation, so canonical docs_subscope resolves the default.

One preview names these consequences:

  1. create the confined child source/documents and local output/by-ID roots;
  2. atomically create only the planned host source and atomically append the associated config record;
  3. run the child builder to create local manifest.json and manage-manifest.json, both {"docs": []};
  4. rebuild the planned host in parent docs and search, which also regenerates Manage and public browser configuration; and
  5. return /docs/?scope=<parent_scope>&doc=<host_doc_id>.

For a public parent, preview also lists the configured public child projection. Create does not publish a child manifest, host, or report there: the existing parent Publish workflow remains the only public snapshot writer.

Preview and result expose the exact collection_target: {scope, sub_scope} and report_host_target: {scope, doc_id}, the host source revision, config association, created/changed/publication path records, both rebuild results, browser-config refresh, and urls.management. urls.public stays empty.

Failure and follow-through contract

The atomic config change is the canonical commit point. Before it, any paths created or staged by this attempt are restored/removed and the response is committed: false; the UI returns to a fresh preview and has no target from which to navigate. An unprovable rollback is reported as indeterminate with the exact affected paths and is never presented as safe to retry.

After config commit, the collection and host are created. A child build, parent docs/search build, browser refresh, index refresh, selection, or navigation failure returns committed: true, retry_create: false, the two exact targets, association, per-stage status, and management URL. Recovery may retry only unfinished build/refresh/select/navigation stages against those identities. It never invokes create again.

Frozen delete contract

Delete preview resolves the config-owned lifecycle object and then the exact parent source <report_host_doc_id>.md. It permits deletion only when:

  • the association is present, strict, and owned by the lifecycle tool;
  • the host exists with the recorded immutable ID and source revision;
  • its report fields still name canonical docs_subscope, local access, and the exact collection; and
  • no second parent document claims that collection.

Missing, detached, ambiguous, or revision-changed state returns allowed: false. A revision change is presented as Report host edited since creation with the exact host target plus recorded/current revisions. Preview does not relabel the edit as lifecycle-owned and apply cannot guess or delete a different host.

An allowed preview lists removal of the exact unchanged host source, child source tree, local manifests/by-ID output, and any configured public snapshot tree; the config association change; removal of the host from parent by-ID, Index, Recent, and search; browser-config regeneration; and navigation to /docs/?scope=<parent_scope>.

Apply recomputes that plan and treats config removal as the delete commit point. Pre-commit failure restores staged owned paths or reports indeterminate state. After commit, cleanup/rebuild/presentation failure returns committed: true, retry_delete: false, the deleted collection/host identities, exact remaining follow-through, and the parent management URL. Recovery never runs collection deletion again.

SSR-2.0 evidence and omissions

The trace inspected the lifecycle service and routes, config normalization and capability projection, child and parent builders, rebuild owners, exact report host resolution, ordinary committed-create recovery, lifecycle client/modal, controller apply callback, and focused lifecycle tests. This checkpoint changes specification and delivery state only. No service, config schema, builder, route, browser behavior, fixture, or test was changed.

SSR-2.0 review gate: the lifecycle plan is frozen. Do not begin SSR-2.1 mutation work without review.

[ ] SSR-2.1 — Service Apply And Empty Projections

  • [ ] Extend write-free preview with the host and projection plan.
  • [ ] Apply configuration, roots, host source, and empty projections through their existing mutation/build owners.
  • [ ] Refresh parent docs/search and browser config without adding child rows to parent discovery.
  • [ ] Preserve exact committed identities across build/follow-through failure.
  • [ ] Cover confinement, collision, stale preview, partial failure, public isolation, and association deletion with focused service tests.

Checkpoint: direct service evidence creates exactly one collection, one host, and complete empty projections. Stop before browser flow.

[ ] SSR-2.2 — Browser Follow-Through

  • [ ] Show host and projection consequences in the existing lifecycle preview/result workflow.
  • [ ] After apply, reload configuration, refresh the parent index, and select only the returned host doc_id.
  • [ ] Mount the empty default report with its correct toolbar and unavailable states.
  • [ ] Prove New and app-level Import use the mounted {scope, sub_scope} with no parent, displayed-document, or URL fallback.

Checkpoint: the newly created collection is immediately usable through its returned report URL.

[ ] SSR-2.3 — External-Local Acceptance And Closeout

  • [ ] Recreate the dotlineform external-local scope and projects sub-scope through the real lifecycle.
  • [ ] Create or import a first Projects child and verify exact refresh and Source entry follow-through.
  • [ ] Verify symmetric deletion and duplicate-prevention failure paths.
  • [ ] Run focused lifecycle, builder, route/module, lint, whitespace, and generated-projection checks.
  • [ ] Update the durable Scope Lifecycle and manifest owners, then stop for review before SSR-3.

Out Of Scope

  • Projects-specific fields, filters, row treatment, or actions;
  • migration of existing manually hosted collections;
  • recursive sub-scopes, rename, or broader scope-lifecycle redesign;
  • automatic public promotion; and
  • changing the default or customisation contract accepted in SSR-1.

Completion Gates

  • One apply creates exactly one configured sub-scope and one indexed host.
  • Empty public-safe and Manage manifests load as normal zero-document state.
  • New and Import receive only the mounted exact collection.
  • Refresh/navigation failure cannot cause duplicate creation.
  • Delete uses the exact stored association and cannot guess a host.
  • Focused external-local acceptance proves the recreated workflow without implying every provider or report has received visual review.
